   519	def rebind_reviewers(runtime, state: ReviewStatus) -> None:
   520	    """Resume: every reviewer receipt is rebound to the one session its launch produced; a reviewer without a receipt
   521	    (its launch was never issued) leaves the run at needs_reconciliation and nothing is launched."""
   522	    combined = state.combined
   523	    partial = combined.get("status") == "needs_reconciliation"
   524	    for reviewer_id in state.ids:
   525	        status = state.statuses[reviewer_id]
   526	        receipt = runtime.directory / f"{review_node(reviewer_id)}.interactive.json"
   527	        if not receipt.exists():
   528	            status.update(status="needs_reconciliation", error=status.get("error") or "No launch receipt; the launch was never issued")
   529	            combined.update(status="needs_reconciliation", error=f"Reviewer {reviewer_id} needs reconciliation; no automatic relaunch")
   530	            state.save()
   531	            raise RuntimeError(f"Reviewer {reviewer_id} needs reconciliation; no automatic relaunch")
   532	        if partial or not status.get("session_id"):
   533	            try:
   534	                bound = runtime.reconcile_reviewer(reviewer_id)
   535	            except Exception as error:
   536	                status.update(status="needs_reconciliation", error=str(error))
   537	                combined.update(status="needs_reconciliation", error=str(error))
   538	                state.save()
   539	                raise
   540	            status.update(session_id=bound["session_id"], background_id=bound.get("background_id"), status="running")
   541	            status.pop("error", None)
   542	            state.save()
   543	    combined["status"] = "running"
   544	    combined.pop("error", None)
   545	    state.save()

   565	def combined_review(runtime, bundle: dict, digest: str, state: ReviewStatus, decisions: dict) -> dict:
   566	    """review.json over the set: unanimous approval passes; any block, unresolved P0/P1, missing or rejected verdict blocks."""
   567	    entries, findings = [], []
   568	    for reviewer_id in state.ids:
   569	        status = state.statuses[reviewer_id]
   570	        decision = decisions.get(reviewer_id)
   571	        entries.append({"reviewer_id": reviewer_id, "session_id": status.get("session_id"),
   572	                        "verdict": decision["verdict"] if decision else None, "accepted_at": status.get("accepted_at") if decision else None})
   573	        if decision:
   574	            findings.extend({**finding, "reviewer": reviewer_id} for finding in decision["findings"])
   575	    blocked = any(reviewer_id not in decisions or decision_blocks(decisions[reviewer_id]) for reviewer_id in state.ids)
   576	    sessions = [entry["session_id"] for entry in entries if entry["session_id"]]
   577	    return {"run_id": bundle["run_id"], "bundle_sha256": digest, "candidate_commit": bundle["candidate_commit"],
   578	            "reviewer": ", ".join(sessions), "independent": True, "verdict": "blocked" if blocked else "approved",
   579	            "findings": findings, "reviewers": entries}

   582	def _decide(runtime, bundle: dict, digest: str, state: ReviewStatus, decisions: dict) -> dict:
   583	    """Persist review.json for any verdict; only unanimous approval without blocking findings passes."""
   584	    review = combined_review(runtime, bundle, digest, state, decisions)
   585	    save_json(runtime.directory / "review.json", review)
   586	    state.record_decisions()
   587	    blockers = [reviewer_id for reviewer_id in state.ids if reviewer_id in decisions and decision_blocks(decisions[reviewer_id])]
   588	    undecided = [reviewer_id for reviewer_id in state.ids if reviewer_id not in decisions]
   589	    if blockers or undecided:
   590	        for reviewer_id in blockers:
   591	            state.statuses[reviewer_id]["status"] = "blocked"  # An approval with an unresolved P0/P1 is contradictory; the run is blocked.
   592	        state.save()
   593	        raise RuntimeError(f"Independent reviewer blocked the candidate ({', '.join(blockers or undecided)})")
   594	    runtime.validate_review(review)
   595	    for status in state.statuses.values():
   596	        status["status"] = "succeeded"
   597	    state.combined.update(status="succeeded", review=review, accepted_at=now())
   598	    state.save()
   599	    return review

   613	    combined = {"transport": "native", "bundle_sha256": digest, "candidate_commit": bundle["candidate_commit"],
   614	                "patch_sha256": digest_file(patch), "status": "launching", "reviewers": [item["reviewer_id"] for item in declared]}
   615	    statuses = {item["reviewer_id"]: {"reviewer_id": item["reviewer_id"], "node_id": review_node(item["reviewer_id"]), "transport": "native",
   616	                                      "launch_token": str(uuid.uuid4()), "bundle_sha256": digest, "candidate_commit": bundle["candidate_commit"],
   617	                                      "status": "pending"} for item in declared}
   618	    state = ReviewStatus(runtime, combined, statuses)
   619	    state.save()
   620	    for reviewer in declared:
   621	        reviewer_id = reviewer["reviewer_id"]
   622	        status = statuses[reviewer_id]
   623	        status["status"] = "launching"
   624	        state.save()
   625	        prompt = review_prompt(runtime, patch, reviewer) + completion_protocol_prompt(runtime, status["launch_token"], digest, bundle["candidate_commit"], reviewer_id)
   626	        try:
   627	            launched = runtime.launch_reviewer(reviewer_id, prompt, status["launch_token"], bundle["candidate_commit"])
   628	        except KeyboardInterrupt:

   630	            if not issued.exists():
   631	                # No launch command was issued for this reviewer. Nothing is guessed either way: the operator reconciles;
   632	                # the reviewers launched before it keep running and nothing is relaunched.
   633	                status.update(status="needs_reconciliation", error="Interrupted before the reviewer launch was issued")
   634	                combined.update(status="needs_reconciliation", error=f"Reviewer {reviewer_id}: interrupted before its launch was issued; nothing is relaunched")
   635	                state.save()
   636	                running = [other for other, item in statuses.items() if item["status"] == "running"]
   637	                if running:
   638	                    runtime.event("review", "interrupted", f"Reviewer {reviewer_id} was never launched; reviewers {', '.join(running)} were NOT stopped and keep running. "
   639	                                  "Resume rebinds them and launches nothing; the run needs reconciliation")
   640	                raise
   641	            # `claude --bg` was issued (settle poll or pane attach interrupted): the session exists or is
   642	            # registering and keeps running. Record what is bound so far; resume binds the rest through
   643	            # reconciliation, never through a relaunch.
   644	            bound = read_json(issued)
   645	            status.update({key: bound[key] for key in ("session_id", "background_id") if bound.get(key)}, status="running")
   646	            combined["status"] = "running"
   647	            state.save()
   648	            runtime.event("review", "interrupted", REVIEW_RESUME_NOTE.format(directory=runtime.directory))
   649	            raise
   650	        except BaseException as error:
   651	            # The launch may or may not have produced a session; only an operator can tell. Never launch again.
   652	            status.update(status="needs_reconciliation", error=str(error))
   653	            combined.update(status="needs_reconciliation", error=str(error))
   654	            state.save()
   655	            raise
   656	        status.update(session_id=launched["session_id"], background_id=launched.get("background_id"), status="running")

   658	    combined["status"] = "running"
   659	    state.save()

   663	def check_independence(runtime, bundle: dict, state: ReviewStatus, rows: list) -> None:
   664	    """Every reviewer is the session its launch bound, and its UUID differs from every worker's and every other reviewer's."""
   665	    worker_ids = {item["session_id"] for item in bundle["snapshots"].values()}

   675	def _accept_native(runtime, bundle: dict, digest: str, state: ReviewStatus) -> dict:
   676	    from .pipeline import digest_file
   677	    cwd = runtime.directory / "review-worktree"
   678	    patch = runtime.directory / "review.diff"
   679	    combined = state.combined
   680	    waited = False
   681	    try:
   682	        decisions = wait_reviews(runtime, state)
   683	        waited = True  # From here a failure refuses the whole review: nothing accepted so far is trusted.
   684	        check_independence(runtime, bundle, state, runtime.sessions.inventory())
   685	        if git(cwd, "rev-parse", "HEAD") != bundle["candidate_commit"] or git(cwd, "status", "--porcelain"):
   686	            raise RuntimeError("Reviewer worktree changed")
   687	        if runtime.validate_bundle()[1] != digest or digest_file(patch) != combined["patch_sha256"]:
   688	            raise RuntimeError("Evidence changed during review")
   689	        review = _decide(runtime, bundle, digest, state, decisions)
   690	    except KeyboardInterrupt:
   691	        # Operator/terminal interruption is not a reviewer failure: the native sessions keep
   692	        # running and `automatic --live` resumes waiting for their completion files.
   693	        runtime.event("review", "interrupted", REVIEW_RESUME_NOTE.format(directory=runtime.directory))
   694	        raise
   695	    except TransientInfraError as error:
   696	        # Claude Code itself was unavailable, not a verdict: the reviewers keep running. The marker lets the
   697	        # next controller re-enter the review node once, which rebinds them and waits again; nothing is relaunched.
   698	        combined["interrupted"] = str(error)
   699	        state.save()
   700	        runtime.event("review", "interrupted", f"{error}. {REVIEW_RESUME_NOTE.format(directory=runtime.directory)}")
   701	        raise
   702	    except BaseException as error:
   703	        # Deadline, blocked session, rejected file or blocked verdict: stop every reviewer so none
   704	        # consumes usage for a run that cannot continue. Nothing is relaunched.
   705	        combined.update(status="blocked", error=str(error))
   706	        state.supersede_running()
   707	        state.save()
   708	        if not waited:
   709	            _record_partial(runtime, bundle, digest, state)
   710	        for failure in stop_reviewers(runtime, state.ids):
   711	            runtime.event("review", "blocked", f"Could not confirm reviewer stop: {failure}")
   712	        raise
   713	    failures = stop_reviewers(runtime, state.ids)
   714	    if failures:
   715	        # The verdict is durable (status succeeded, review.json written); only a stop is unconfirmed.
   716	        # review_candidate retries it on resume before handing the accepted review back.
   717	        runtime.event("review", "running", f"Could not confirm reviewer stop: {'; '.join(failures)}; resume retries the stop")
   718	        raise RuntimeError("; ".join(failures))
   719	    return review

   891	class Timeline:
   892	    """Prints the run's timeline in the supervisor's terminal while it supervises, so a resumed run is visibly alive.
   893	
   894	    The automatic-step children and other commands append the events, so this follows events.jsonl rather than an
   895	    in-process writer. A line counts once its newline is written, and a sequence number prints at most once, however
   896	    often the controller restarts. Entering prints a header and the last few events; leaving prints whatever the last
   897	    controller recorded, before the caller's result or error.
   898	    """
   899	
   900	    def __init__(self, directory: Path):
   901	        self.directory = directory
   902	        self.path = directory / "events.jsonl"
   903	        self.offset = 0
   904	        self.printed = 0  # The highest sequence number shown or skipped.
   905	        self.stop = threading.Event()
   906	        self.follower = threading.Thread(target=self.follow, name="timeline", daemon=True)
   907	
   908	    def read(self) -> list[dict]:
   909	        """Events completed since the last read; a partly written last line waits for its newline."""
   910	        try:
   911	            with self.path.open("rb") as handle:
   912	                if os.fstat(handle.fileno()).st_size < self.offset:
   913	                    self.offset = 0  # Replaced, not appended: the sequence numbers skip what was shown.
   914	                handle.seek(self.offset)
   915	                data = handle.read()
   916	        except OSError:
   917	            return []
   918	        data = data[:data.rfind(b"\n") + 1]
   919	        self.offset += len(data)
   920	        events = []
   921	        for line in data.splitlines():
   922	            try:
   923	                event = json.loads(line)
   924	            except ValueError:
   925	                continue
   926	            if isinstance(event, dict) and type(event.get("sequence")) is int and event["sequence"] > self.printed:
   927	                events.append(event)
   928	        return events
   929	
   930	    def show(self, events: list[dict]) -> None:
   931	        for event in events:
   932	            print(timeline_line(event), flush=True)
   933	            self.printed = max(self.printed, event["sequence"])
   934	
   935	    def poll(self) -> None:
   936	        self.show(self.read())
   937	
   938	    def follow(self) -> None:
   939	        while not self.stop.wait(TIMELINE_POLL_SECONDS):
   940	            self.poll()
   941	
   942	    def __enter__(self):
   943	        events = self.read()
   944	        recent = events[-TIMELINE_TAIL:]
   945	        print(f"Supervising {self.directory}; timeline in UTC, "
   946	              + (f"the last {len(recent)} of {len(events)} events:" if events else "no events yet."), flush=True)
   947	        self.printed = max([self.printed, *(event["sequence"] for event in events)])  # The earlier ones are skipped.
   948	        self.show(recent)
   949	        self.follower.start()
   950	        return self
   951	
   952	    def __exit__(self, *_):
   953	        self.stop.set()
   954	        self.follower.join()
   955	        self.poll()

   218	class TransientInfraError(RuntimeError):
   219	    """Claude Code itself is unavailable: an update is replacing the binary, or the background service is restarting.
   220	
   221	    It is not a verdict on any session, so the automatic controller stops nothing on it and exits resumable.
   222	    Raised by type at the source (run_claude and friends, the session inventory); never classified from message text.

   229	def claude_env(env: dict | None = None) -> dict:
   230	    """The environment of every Claude process the controller starts: `env` (default: this process's) with the auto-updater off.
   231	
   232	    An update replaces the binary under every running session and restarts the background service, so a run never
   233	    updates Claude Code underneath itself; operators update between runs. A `claude --bg` session is not started by
   234	    the controller: it takes the setting from background_settings.

   243	    service's own environment plus an allowlist of the helper's (provider, model, config, endpoint and PATH variables),
   244	    so claude_env reaches the session only when this run happened to start the service. The helper's arguments do

   250	def wait_out_update(start, grace: float, sleep=None, retry_output=None):
   251	    """`start()` (it runs or starts one `claude` command), repeated while a Claude Code update is in progress.
   252	
   253	    An update replaces the installed binary: for a moment the command is missing (ENOENT), half written (ENOEXEC)
   254	    or busy (ETXTBSY), and the exec fails before anything runs. That is repeated every 2 seconds for `grace`
   255	    seconds, then raised as TransientInfraError. `retry_output`, when given, marks a command that only reads (the
   256	    session inventory), so running it again is harmless: an answer it rejects (the restarting background service
   257	    exits nonzero or lists nothing) and a timeout are repeated too, a timeout spending its own seconds of the
   258	    grace; once the grace is spent the last answer is returned, or the timeout raised. Any other failure is raised
   259	    at once, and a command that ran is never repeated without `retry_output`: a launch or a print job never starts twice.
   260	    """
   261	    sleep = sleep or time.sleep
   262	    waited = 0.0
   263	    while True:
   264	        try:
   265	            result = start()
   266	        except OSError as error:
   267	            if not (isinstance(error, FileNotFoundError) or error.errno in UPDATE_ERRNOS):
   268	                raise
   269	            if waited >= grace:
   270	                raise TransientInfraError(f"Claude Code unavailable for {grace:g}s ({error}); an update may be replacing it") from error
   271	        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as error:
   272	            waited += error.timeout
   273	            if retry_output is None or waited >= grace:
   274	                raise
   275	        else:
   276	            if retry_output is None or not retry_output(result) or waited >= grace:
   277	                return result
   278	        sleep(2)
   279	        waited += 2

   282	def run_claude(command: list[str], *, grace: float = CLAUDE_MISSING_GRACE_SECONDS, sleep=None, retry_output=None,
   283	               **kwargs) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
   284	    """`subprocess.run` for a `claude` command, with the auto-updater off, that waits out an update in progress (wait_out_update)."""
   285	    kwargs["env"] = claude_env(kwargs.get("env"))
   286	    return wait_out_update(lambda: subprocess.run(command, **kwargs), grace, sleep, retry_output)

   295	def stale_claude_processes(proc: Path = Path("/proc")) -> list[dict]:
   296	    """Running Claude Code processes whose executable an update deleted: `{pid, cwd, command}` each, by pid.
   297	
   298	    Such a long-lived session keeps seeing a newer version and reinstalls Claude Code, which makes `claude` briefly
   299	    missing for every other caller. Linux only: without /proc, or for an entry that cannot be read, nothing is reported.
   300	    """
   301	    try:
   302	        entries = [entry for entry in proc.iterdir() if entry.name.isdigit()]
   303	    except OSError:
   304	        return []
   305	    found = []
   306	    for entry in sorted(entries, key=lambda item: int(item.name)):
   307	        try:
   308	            executable = os.readlink(entry / "exe")
   309	            if not executable.endswith(" (deleted)") or "claude" not in executable.lower():
   310	                continue
   311	            cwd = os.readlink(entry / "cwd")
   312	            command = (entry / "cmdline").read_bytes().rstrip(b"\0").replace(b"\0", b" ").decode(errors="replace")
   313	        except OSError:
   314	            continue
   315	        found.append({"pid": int(entry.name), "cwd": cwd, "command": command})
   316	    return found

   319	def stale_claude_warning(proc: Path = Path("/proc")) -> str:

   321	    stale = stale_claude_processes(proc)
   322	    if not stale:
   323	        return ""
   324	    return "\n".join([f"Warning: {len(stale)} running Claude Code process(es) still run an executable that an update deleted. "
   325	                      "These long-lived sessions keep reinstalling Claude Code, which makes `claude` briefly unavailable to this "
   326	                      "run; restart them before the run:",
   327	                      *(f"  pid {item['pid']} in {item['cwd']}: {item['command']}" for item in stale)])

   335	    try:

   381	                   "--mcp-config", '{"mcpServers":{}}', "--tools", tools,
   382	                   "--permission-mode", "acceptEdits" if self.plan["allow_edits"] else "dontAsk",

+    return f"Reviewer {node}" if is_review_node(node) else f"Worker {node}"

+def process_alive(pid) -> bool:
+    """A PID from the session's own verified row; no PID (nothing attached yet) is never alive.
+
+    kill(pid, 0) also answers for a process that has exited but is not collected yet (a zombie,
+    for as long as its parent or, for an adopted session, init has not reaped it).
+    """
+    if not isinstance(pid, int) or pid <= 0:
+        return False
+    try:
+        os.kill(pid, 0)
+    except OSError:
+        return False
+    try:
+        return Path(f"/proc/{pid}/stat").read_text().rsplit(")", 1)[1].split()[0] != "Z"
+    except (OSError, IndexError):
+        return True  # No /proc: kill(pid, 0) is all there is.
+

+def recorded_stop(directory: Path, node: str) -> dict | None:
+    """The controller's stop of this node's session as `{time, reason, confirmed, background_id}`, or None when it recorded none.
+
+    `<node>.stop.json` is written before `claude stop` runs, so an attach that the stop itself ends
+    already finds it; an unconfirmed intent counts too, since only the controller retries that stop.
+    The time and reason come from the stop's timeline event (for workers stopped after a blocked
+    wait, from that block), else from the marker.
+    """
+    marker = directory / f"{node}.stop.json"
+    if not marker.is_file():
+        return None
+    try:
+        intent = read_json(marker)
+        confirmed = intent.get("stopped") is True
+    except (ValueError, AttributeError):
+        intent, confirmed = {}, False
+    when = datetime.fromtimestamp(marker.stat().st_mtime, timezone.utc)
+    reason = "stop recorded" if confirmed else "stop requested, not yet confirmed"
+    path = directory / "events.jsonl"
+    lines = path.read_text(errors="replace").splitlines() if confirmed and path.is_file() else []
+    events = []
+    for line in lines:
+        try:
+            events.append(json.loads(line))
+        except ValueError:
+            continue  # A line the controller was still writing.
+    phase, prefix = (REVIEW, f"{node_title(node)} session stopped") if is_review_node(node) else ("freeze", "Native workers stopped")
+    for index in range(len(events) - 1, -1, -1):
+        event = events[index]
+        if event.get("node") == phase and event.get("status") == "stopped" and str(event.get("message", "")).startswith(prefix):
+            when, reason = datetime.fromisoformat(event["time"]), event["message"]
+            previous = events[index - 1] if index else {}
+            if previous.get("node") == "controller" and previous.get("status") == "blocked":
+                reason = f"the run blocked: {previous['message']}"
+            break
+    return {"time": when.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S UTC"), "reason": reason, "confirmed": confirmed,
+            "background_id": intent.get("background_id")}
+
+
+def stop_reported(directory: Path, node: str) -> bool:
+    """Whether the controller recorded a stop of this node's session; if so, one line says so."""
+    stop = recorded_stop(directory, node)
+    if stop is None:
+        return False
+    if stop["confirmed"]:
+        message = f"{node_title(node)} was stopped by the controller at {stop['time']} ({stop['reason']}); nothing to attach."
+    else:
+        message = (f"The controller is stopping {node} (requested at {stop['time']}, not yet confirmed); not attaching. "
+                   f"Inspect it with `claude logs {stop['background_id']}` or `claude attach {stop['background_id']}`.")
+    print(message, file=sys.stderr, flush=True)
+    return True

+def observe(sessions: InteractiveSessions, node: str, attached: dict | None) -> dict:
+    """The session's verified live row; SessionGap while a restarting service cannot confirm it yet.
+
+    Only a background id verified live and attached before (`attached`, its row then) earns that wait,
+    whatever became of its PID, since an update respawns the session under a new one. How the listing
+    itself fails (a missing CLI, a timeout, a non-zero exit, output it cannot parse) is Claude Code's
+    business and every such failure is a gap, as are a row still registering its PID or in a state
+    between two processes, a listing without the id while the attached process lives, and (ProcessEnded)
+    a row still listing a PID whose process ended or a listing without the id once it ended. A first
+    attach, a terminal state and every identity refusal fail at once: nothing is attached without a
+    verified live row.
+    """
+    try:
+        rows = sessions.inventory()
+    except Exception as error:
+        if attached is None:
+            raise
+        raise SessionGap(str(error)) from error
+    try:
+        row = sessions.locate(node, rows)
+    except RuntimeError as error:
+        if attached is None:
+            raise
+        if str(error).startswith(PROCESS_ENDED):
+            raise ProcessEnded(PROCESS_ENDED) from error
+        terminal = any(listed.get("id") == attached["id"] and listed.get("state") in TERMINAL_STATES for listed in rows)
+        if terminal or not str(error).startswith(TRANSIENT_REFUSALS):
+            raise
+        raise SessionGap(str(error)) from error
+    if row is None:
+        if attached is None:
+            raise RuntimeError("Session unavailable; refusing implicit restart")
+        if not process_alive(attached["pid"]):
+            # Without --all `claude agents` omits a finished (`done`) session that has no process: an idle one between
+            # the two processes of an update's respawn, or one that ended.
+            raise ProcessEnded("Session unavailable; refusing implicit restart")
+        raise SessionGap(f"`claude agents` does not list {attached['id']}")
+    if not process_alive(row["pid"]):  # A zombie passes locate's kill(pid, 0).
+        raise ProcessEnded(PROCESS_ENDED) if attached is not None else RuntimeError(PROCESS_ENDED)
+    return row
+

+def attach_one(sessions: InteractiveSessions, node: str, *, clock=time.monotonic, sleep=time.sleep) -> None:
+    """Attach one session in this terminal, and attach it again after a lost connection.
+
+    `claude attach` exits 0 when the operator detaches (Ctrl+Z, or ← to the agent view) or the session
+    ended, and non-zero when it loses the background service. After each attach the run's own records
+    decide: a stop the controller recorded ends attach-one with one line, a live session the controller
+    has not stopped is attached again after a bounded backoff (also after exit 0 when the service respawned
+    it under a new PID: a detach never changes the PID), and a session gone without a recorded stop is
+    refused. `claude attach` would wake a missing session, so only an exact live row is ever attached.
+    """
+    failures, attached = 0, None  # attached: the row of the last attach
+    ended = None  # How the last attach ended ("detached", "interrupted" or "lost"); None once decided, or before the first.
+    dead_since = last_error = None  # When a row was first seen listing an ended process; what made the latest attempt fail.
+    while True:
+        if stop_reported(sessions.directory, node):
+            return
+        try:
+            row = observe(sessions, node, attached)
+        except ProcessEnded as gap:
+            # A respawn lists its new PID within seconds; a session that keeps missing a live process has ended.
+            now = clock()
+            dead_since = now if dead_since is None else dead_since
+            if now - dead_since >= DEAD_PID_GRACE_SECONDS:
+                raise
+            row, last_error = None, str(gap)
+        except SessionGap as gap:
+            row, last_error = None, str(gap)
+        else:
+            dead_since = None
+        respawned = row is not None and ended is not None and row["pid"] != attached["pid"]
+        if ended == "interrupted" or (ended == "detached" and row is not None and not respawned):
+            return  # The operator detached or interrupted the attach; the session keeps running.
+        if row is not None and ended is None:
+            if stop_reported(sessions.directory, node):
+                return  # The controller's stop intent precedes `claude stop`: a session it is stopping is never attached.
+            attached, started = row, clock()
+            try:
+                code = subprocess.run([sessions.executable, "attach", row["id"]], cwd=sessions.node_worktree(node)).returncode
+                failure = f"`claude attach` exited {code}"
+            except OSError as error:
+                code, failure = 1, str(error)  # An update is replacing the CLI itself: retried like a lost connection.
+            if clock() - started >= ATTACH_STABLE_SECONDS:
+                failures = 0  # It was connected for a while: its end starts a new count.
+            # An attach the operator interrupted (Ctrl+C: 130, or killed by SIGINT) is never retried.
+            ended = "interrupted" if code in (130, -signal.SIGINT) else "detached" if code == 0 else "lost"
+            if ended == "lost":
+                last_error = failure
+            continue  # The records decide first: a stop, or a session that ended, is never waited for.
+        failures += 1
+        if failures >= REATTACH_LIMIT:
+            raise RuntimeError(f"Gave up reattaching {node} ({attached['id']}) after {REATTACH_LIMIT} attempts in a row; the session may still "
+                               f"be running. Rerun attach-one once `claude agents` lists it again"
+                               + (f"; last error: {last_error}" if last_error else ""))
+        delay = min(2 ** failures, REATTACH_MAX_DELAY)
+        if respawned:
+            print(f"The background service respawned {node} ({attached['id']}) as PID {row['pid']}; reattaching in {delay}s…",
+                  file=sys.stderr, flush=True)
+        elif ended == "lost":
+            print(f"Lost the connection to {node} ({attached['id']}); the background service may be restarting. Reattaching in {delay}s…",
+                  file=sys.stderr, flush=True)
+        else:
+            print(f"The background service does not list {node} ({attached['id']}) yet; retrying in {delay}s…", file=sys.stderr, flush=True)
+        if row is not None or ended != "detached":
+            ended = None  # A detach stays undecided until a row shows whether the PID changed.
+        sleep(delay)
+

   304	    directory = sessions.directory

   341	def allocate_reviewer_pane(sessions: InteractiveSessions, mapping: dict, mapping_path: Path, node: str = REVIEW) -> None:
   342	    """A reviewer pane splits right of the previous pane: the last lane's for the first reviewer, then each reviewer's predecessor."""

   344	    reviewers = review_nodes(sessions.plan)

   352	def attach_pane(sessions: InteractiveSessions, mapping: dict, mapping_path: Path, node: str, session_id: str) -> None:

     2	
     3	Frozen snapshots never change, so a lane blocked at `verify_<lane>` or at the combined candidate used to need a new

   163	            if folder.is_dir() and not (folder / "packet.json").exists():
   164	                raise ValueError(f"Interrupted check at {folder}; use retry --phase {phase} --node {node}")
   165	    failed = [task.name for task in state.tasks if task.error and task.name in state.next]
   166	    verifies = {f"verify_{node}" for node in runtime.workers}
   167	    if failed == ["candidate"] and tuple(state.next) == ("candidate",):
   168	        phase, nodes = "candidate", runtime.workers
   169	    elif failed and set(state.next) <= verifies:
   170	        phase, nodes = "worker", [name.removeprefix("verify_") for name in failed]
   171	    else:
   172	        raise ValueError("The run did not stop at a check verdict of the candidate or a verify_<lane> step; inspect, then retry")
   173	    packets = []
   174	    for node in nodes:
   175	        attempt = raw_attempt(directory, phase, node)
   176	        path = directory / "verification" / phase / node / str(attempt) / "packet.json"
   177	        packet = read_json(path) if path.exists() else None
   178	        if packet and packet["gate"]["status"] == "blocked":
   179	            packets.append({"phase": phase, "node_id": node, "path": str(path.relative_to(directory)), "sha256": digest_file(path),
   180	                            "attempt": attempt, "output_commit": packet["expected"]["output_commit"], "reasons": packet["gate"]["reasons"]})
   181	    if not packets:
   182	        raise ValueError("The failed step has no blocked packet at its current attempt, so it is not a check verdict "
   183	                         "(an infrastructure error, a cherry-pick conflict, a partial candidate); inspect, then retry")
   184	    return {"step": "candidate" if phase == "candidate" else ", ".join(failed), "packets": packets}

   187	def check_source(runtime) -> None:
   188	    """integrate()'s own checks, done early: a fix committed on the pinned source branch is outside every gate."""
   189	    plan, repo = runtime.plan, Path(runtime.plan["repository"])
   190	    elsewhere = f"commit fixes in a repair workspace (repair {runtime.directory} <lane> --workspace), never in the source checkout"
   191	    branch = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(repo), "symbolic-ref", "-q", "--short", "HEAD"], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip()
   192	    if branch != plan["source_branch"]:
   193	        raise ValueError(f"The source checkout is on {branch or 'a detached HEAD'}, not the run's branch {plan['source_branch']}; {elsewhere}")
   194	    head = git(repo, "rev-parse", "HEAD")
   195	    if head != plan["base_commit"]:
   196	        raise ValueError(f"The source branch {branch} moved from the run's base {plan['base_commit'][:8]} to {head[:8]}, which integration "
   197	                         f"refuses; {elsewhere}")
   198	    if git(repo, "status", "--porcelain"):
   199	        raise ValueError(f"The source checkout has uncommitted changes, which integration refuses; {elsewhere}")

   202	def fork_point(graph, config, runtime, previous: dict, checkpoint_id: str | None = None):
   203	    """The freeze boundary: the newest checkpoint whose next step is exactly the verify fan-out (the handoff's output or the
   204	    previous repair's fork), or the recorded one. Its snapshots must be snapshots.json overlaid by the applied repairs."""
   205	    fan_out = {f"verify_{node}" for node in runtime.workers}
   206	    fork = next((item for item in graph.get_state_history(config)
   207	                 if (item.config["configurable"]["checkpoint_id"] == checkpoint_id if checkpoint_id else set(item.next) == fan_out)), None)
   208	    if fork is None or set(fork.next) != fan_out or fork.values.get("snapshots") != previous:
   209	        raise RuntimeError("Contradictory run state: no freeze-boundary checkpoint holds snapshots.json plus the applied repairs; inspect")
   210	    return fork

   213	def blocked_run(runtime, graph, config, applied: list[dict]) -> tuple:
   214	    """Every state refusal. Returns the head, the blocked step, the fork point and the effective snapshots."""
   215	    state = graph.get_state(config)
   216	    check_before_review(runtime, state)
   217	    if len(applied) >= MAX_REPAIRS:
   218	        raise ValueError(f"{len(applied)} repairs are already applied to this run (at most {MAX_REPAIRS}); start a revised run")
   219	    # A failed verify superstep writes no checkpoint: a continuation that failed a lane's check again leaves the fork as
   220	    # the head with the error pending. Only a fork nothing has failed from is a repair not yet continued.
   221	    if applied and state.config["configurable"]["checkpoint_id"] == applied[-1]["head_after"] and not any(task.error for task in state.tasks):
   222	        raise ValueError(f"Repair {applied[-1]['n']} is applied and the run has not continued from it; an applied repair is not "
   223	                         f"replaced. Continue with: {continuation(runtime)}")
   224	    blocked = blocked_step(runtime, state)
   225	    check_source(runtime)
   226	    previous = effective_snapshots(runtime.directory, applied)
   227	    return state, blocked, fork_point(graph, config, runtime, previous), previous

   232	def resolve_commit(repo: Path, value: str) -> str:
   233	    result = None if value.startswith("-") else subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(repo), "rev-parse", "--verify", "--quiet", f"{value}^{{commit}}"],
   234	                                                                capture_output=True, text=True)
   235	    if result is None or result.returncode != 0 or not result.stdout.strip():
   236	        raise ValueError(f"--commit {value} is not a commit in {repo}")
   237	    return result.stdout.strip()

   240	def descends(repo: Path, ancestor: str, commit: str) -> bool:
   241	    return subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(repo), "merge-base", "--is-ancestor", ancestor, commit], capture_output=True).returncode == 0

   244	def changed_paths(repo: Path, old: str, new: str) -> list[str]:
   245	    output = subprocess.check_output(["git", "-C", str(repo), "diff-tree", "-r", "--no-renames", "--name-only", "-z", old, new]).decode()
   246	    return sorted(filter(None, output.split("\0")))

   249	def lane_owner(runtime, path: str) -> str | None:
   250	    """The declared lane (selected or excluded) whose owned paths hold `path`; lanes never overlap."""

   252	                 if any(owns(path, safe_path(prefix)) for prefix in worker["owned_paths"])), None)

   255	def tree_entries(repo: Path, commit: str, paths: list[str]) -> dict:
   256	    """`path -> ls-tree line` for the paths present in `commit`."""
   257	    if not paths:
   258	        return {}
   259	    output = subprocess.check_output(["git", "-C", str(repo), "ls-tree", "-r", "-z", commit, "--", *paths]).decode()
   260	    return {line.split("\t", 1)[1]: line for line in filter(None, output.split("\0"))}

   263	def overlay_tree(repo: Path, snapshot: str, paths: list[str], entries: dict) -> str:
   264	    """The snapshot's tree with `paths` as the fix has them (removed where it deletes them), built in a private index.
   265	
   266	    The index lives in a temporary directory: the source checkout's own index and the run directory are never written.
   267	    """
   268	    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="workflow-repair-") as scratch:
   269	        env = {**os.environ, "GIT_INDEX_FILE": str(Path(scratch) / "index")}
   270	        command = ["git", "-C", str(repo)]
   271	        subprocess.run([*command, "read-tree", snapshot], env=env, check=True, capture_output=True)
   272	        removed = [path for path in paths if path not in entries]
   273	        if removed:
   274	            subprocess.run([*command, "update-index", "--force-remove", "--", *removed], env=env, check=True, capture_output=True)
   275	        present = "".join(entries[path] + "\0" for path in paths if path in entries)
   276	        if present:
   277	            subprocess.run([*command, "update-index", "-z", "--index-info"], input=present.encode(), env=env, check=True, capture_output=True)
   278	        return subprocess.check_output([*command, "write-tree"], env=env, text=True).strip()

   281	def derive(runtime, lanes: list[str], source: str, phase: str, previous: dict) -> dict:
   282	    """The fix's base, the files of each named lane and each lane's new tree, checked with freeze's rules. Read only
   283	    (Git writes the trees' objects, which nothing references)."""
   284	    directory, repo = runtime.directory, Path(runtime.plan["repository"])
   285	    generation = len(applied_repairs(directory))
   286	    saved = [candidate_paths(directory, number)[0] for number in range(generation + 1)]
   287	    commits = [read_json(path)["commit"] if path.exists() else None for path in saved]
   288	    current, older = commits[-1], [commit for commit in commits[:-1] if commit]
   289	    if phase == "candidate" and current and descends(repo, current, source):
   290	        base_kind, base = "candidate", current
   291	    elif any(descends(repo, commit, source) for commit in older):
   292	        raise ValueError(f"--commit {source[:8]} is on the candidate of an earlier generation, not the current one ({(current or 'none')[:8]}); "
   293	                         "commit the fix on the current candidate")
   294	    elif any(descends(repo, previous[lane]["commit"], source) for lane in lanes):
   295	        if len(lanes) > 1:
   296	            raise ValueError("A fix on a lane snapshot repairs one lane only: overlaying base content onto another lane would discard its "
   297	                             "changes. Commit a fix spanning lanes on the failing candidate (repair <run> <lanes> --workspace)")
   298	        base_kind, base = "snapshot", previous[lanes[0]]["commit"]
   299	    else:
   300	        bases = ([f"the current candidate {current[:8]}"] if phase == "candidate" and current else []) + \

300	        bases = ([f"the current candidate {current[:8]}"] if phase == "candidate" and current else []) + \
   301	                [f"the {lane} snapshot {previous[lane]['commit'][:8]}" for lane in lanes]
   302	        raise ValueError(f"--commit {source[:8]} descends from neither {' nor '.join(bases)}; make it in a repair workspace "
   303	                         f"(repair {directory} <lane> --workspace)")
   304	    fix = changed_paths(repo, base, source)
   305	    for path in fix:
   306	        safe_path(path)
   307	        owner = lane_owner(runtime, path)
   308	        if owner is None:
   309	            raise ValueError(f"The fix changes {path}, which no lane owns")
   310	        if owner in runtime.excluded:
   311	            raise ValueError(f"Ownership violation: the fix changes {path}, owned by excluded lane {owner}")
   312	        if owner not in lanes:
   313	            raise ValueError(f"The fix changes {path}, owned by lane {owner}, which this repair does not name; name {owner} too or leave the file alone")
   314	    entries = tree_entries(repo, source, fix)
   315	    for path, line in entries.items():
   316	        mode = line.split(" ", 1)[0]
   317	        if mode == "120000":
   318	            raise ValueError(f"Symlink changes require manual review before snapshot: {path}")
   319	        if mode == "160000":
   320	            raise ValueError(f"Gitlink (submodule) changes are refused: {path}")
   321	    result = {}
   322	    for lane in lanes:
   323	        snapshot = previous[lane]["commit"]
   324	        paths = [path for path in fix if lane_owner(runtime, path) == lane]
   325	        tree = overlay_tree(repo, snapshot, paths, entries)
   326	        if tree == git(repo, "rev-parse", f"{snapshot}^{{tree}}"):
   327	            raise ValueError(f"The fix changes nothing in the {lane} snapshot {snapshot[:8]}: a repair is not a retry (use retry for a transient failure)")
   328	        changed = changed_paths(repo, runtime.plan["base_commit"], tree)
   329	        runtime.check_ownership(lane, changed)
   330	        result[lane] = {"previous_commit": snapshot, "fix_files": paths, "tree": tree, "changed_files": changed}
   331	    return {"base_kind": base_kind, "base_commit": base, "lanes": result,
   332	            "expected_candidate_tree": git(repo, "rev-parse", f"{source}^{{tree}}") if base_kind == "candidate" else None}

   335	def attempt_targets(directory: Path, lanes: list[str], workers: list[str]) -> dict:
   336	    """The worker phase of each repaired lane and the candidate phase of every lane that has a candidate attempt directory
   337	    start past their counter and past every existing attempt: nothing is moved, and no attempt directory is reused."""
   338	    targets = {}
   339	    for phase, nodes in (("worker", lanes), ("candidate", workers)):
   340	        for node in nodes:
   341	            existing = attempt_directories(directory, phase, node)
   342	            if phase == "worker" or existing:
   343	                targets[f"{phase}:{node}"] = max(raw_attempt(directory, phase, node), max(existing, default=0) + 1)
   344	    return targets

   359	def commit_snapshots(runtime, entry: dict, derived: dict) -> None:
   360	    """S2: one commit per lane, parent the run's base, dated at the recorded time so a rerun makes the same commit; refs keep
   361	    it and the operator's commit. Beside refs/workflow/, where no lane id can name them."""
   362	    repo, plan = runtime.plan["repository"], runtime.plan
   363	    stamp = f"{int(datetime.fromisoformat(entry['recorded_at']).timestamp())} +0000"
   364	    env = {**commit_env(), "GIT_AUTHOR_DATE": stamp, "GIT_COMMITTER_DATE": stamp}
   365	    prefix = f"refs/workflow-repair/{hashlib.sha256(str(runtime.directory).encode()).hexdigest()[:16]}/{entry['n']}"
   366	    for lane, item in derived["lanes"].items():
   367	        commit = plan["base_commit"]  # As freeze records a lane that changed nothing.
   368	        if item["changed_files"]:
   369	            commit = subprocess.check_output(["git", "-C", repo, "-c", "commit.gpgsign=false", "commit-tree", item["tree"], "-p", plan["base_commit"],
   370	                                              "-m", f"Workflow {plan['run_id']}: {lane} repair {entry['n']}"], env=env, text=True).strip()
   371	        item["commit"] = commit
   372	        subprocess.run(["git", "-C", repo, "update-ref", f"{prefix}/{lane}", commit], check=True)
   373	    subprocess.run(["git", "-C", repo, "update-ref", f"{prefix}/source_commit", entry["source_commit"]], check=True)

   380	    save_entry(runtime.directory, entry)

   395	def fork_run(graph, config, runtime, entry: dict, fork, snapshots: dict) -> str:
   396	    """S5: exactly one new checkpoint, as if `handoff` had written the repaired snapshots, forked from the freeze boundary.
   397	
   398	    `fork.config` carries its checkpoint_id, and pending writes are not carried into a fork: the failed step's trigger
   399	    and the old packets stay on the failed branch. The bare thread config would update the failed head instead, which
   400	    runs the candidate beside the verifies with the new snapshots and the old packets. Neither the handoff's interrupt,
   401	    nor freeze, nor the worker stop runs; only its edges fire.
   402	    """
   403	    head = graph.get_state(config)
   404	    if head.config["configurable"]["checkpoint_id"] == entry["head_before"]:
   405	        graph.update_state(fork.config, {"snapshots": snapshots}, as_node="handoff")
   406	        head = graph.get_state(config)
   407	    elif not (head.parent_config and head.parent_config["configurable"]["checkpoint_id"] == entry["fork_from"] and head.metadata.get("source") == "update"):
   408	        raise RuntimeError(f"Checkpoint moved since repair {entry['n']} was recorded (head {head.config['configurable']['checkpoint_id']}); inspect")
   409	    if set(head.next) != {f"verify_{node}" for node in runtime.workers} or any(task.error for task in head.tasks) or head.values.get("snapshots") != snapshots:
   410	        raise RuntimeError(f"Contradictory run state after the fork of repair {entry['n']}: the next step is not the verify fan-out; inspect")
   411	    return head.config["configurable"]["checkpoint_id"]

   414	def finish_repair(runtime, graph, config, entry: dict, head_after: str) -> None:
   415	    """S6: the timeline, the entry `applied`, then the report and run-state.json. Events a crash duplicated are harmless."""
   416	    directory, n = runtime.directory, entry["n"]
   417	    answers = " ".join(f"Answers {packet['phase']}/{packet['node_id']} attempt {packet['attempt']}: {'; '.join(packet['reasons'])}."
   418	                       for packet in entry["blocked"]["packets"])
   419	    for lane, item in entry["lanes"].items():
   420	        runtime.event(f"verify_{lane}", "paused", f"Repair {n} by the operator: snapshot {item['commit'][:8]} = {item['previous_commit'][:8]} + "
   421	                                                  f"{entry['source_commit'][:8]} on {entry['base_kind']} {entry['base_commit'][:8]} "
   422	                                                  f"({', '.join(item['fix_files'])}). Reason: {entry['reason']}. {answers} "
   423	                                                  f"Continue with {continuation(runtime, 'python')}")
   424	    superseded = candidate_paths(directory, n - 1)[0]
   425	    if superseded.exists():
   426	        runtime.event("candidate", "paused", f"Repair {n} supersedes combined revision {read_json(superseded)['commit'][:8]}; "
   427	                                             f"candidate-{n} is built after the lanes re-verify")
   428	    runtime.event("controller", "running", f"Repair {n} applied: checkpoint forked from {entry['fork_from'][:8]} (after handoff); attempts "
   429	                                           + ", ".join(f"{key} {value}" for key, value in entry["attempt_targets"].items()))
   430	    entry.update(status="applied", applied_at=now(), head_after=head_after)
   431	    save_entry(directory, entry)
   432	    report(runtime, graph.get_state(config))

   435	def apply_repair(runtime, graph, config, lanes: list[str], commit: str, reason: str, dry_run: bool) -> None:
   436	    directory, repo = runtime.directory, Path(runtime.plan["repository"])
   437	    source = resolve_commit(repo, commit)
   438	    entries = load_repairs(directory)
   439	    applied = [entry for entry in entries if entry["status"] == "applied"]
   440	    recorded = next((entry for entry in entries if entry["status"] == "recorded"), None)
   441	    if recorded is None:
   442	        state, blocked, fork, previous = blocked_run(runtime, graph, config, applied)
   443	    elif list(recorded["lanes"]) != lanes or recorded["source_commit"] != source or recorded["reason"] != reason:
   444	        raise RuntimeError(f"Repair {recorded['n']} is recorded but not applied; only the identical command completes it: "
   445	                           f"{repair_command(directory, recorded)}")
   446	    else:
   447	        # Completing a crashed repair: the head may already be its fork, so the recorded step and fork point stand.
   448	        check_before_review(runtime, graph.get_state(config))
   449	        check_source(runtime)
   450	        blocked, previous = recorded["blocked"], effective_snapshots(directory, applied)
   451	        fork = fork_point(graph, config, runtime, previous, recorded["fork_from"])
   452	    derived = derive(runtime, lanes, source, blocked["packets"][0]["phase"], previous)
   453	    if recorded is None:
   454	        targets = attempt_targets(directory, lanes, runtime.workers)
   455	        entry = {"n": len(entries) + 1, "status": "recorded", "mode": "commit", "reason": reason, "recorded_at": now(), "blocked": blocked,
   456	                 "source_commit": source, "base_kind": derived["base_kind"], "base_commit": derived["base_commit"],
   457	                 "expected_candidate_tree": derived["expected_candidate_tree"],
   458	                 "lanes": {lane: {"previous_commit": item["previous_commit"], "fix_files": item["fix_files"]} for lane, item in derived["lanes"].items()},
   459	                 "attempt_targets": targets, "attempt_floors": dict(targets),
   460	                 "fork_from": fork.config["configurable"]["checkpoint_id"], "head_before": state.config["configurable"]["checkpoint_id"]}
   461	    else:
   462	        entry = recorded
   463	        if any(entry[key] != derived[key] for key in ("base_kind", "base_commit", "expected_candidate_tree")) or \
   464	                any(entry["lanes"][lane]["fix_files"] != item["fix_files"] for lane, item in derived["lanes"].items()):
   465	            raise RuntimeError(f"Contradictory run state: repair {entry['n']} no longer derives the snapshots it recorded; inspect")
   466	    if dry_run:
   467	        print(f"Dry run of repair {entry['n']} (nothing written): {reason}\n{describe(entry, derived, dry_run)}\n"
   468	              f"  fork from checkpoint {entry['fork_from']} (after handoff)\nApply: the same command without --dry-run. Then continue with: {continuation(runtime)}")
   469	        return
   470	    if recorded is None:
   471	        record_repair(directory, entry)                                                   # S1
   472	    commit_snapshots(runtime, entry, derived)                                             # S2
   473	    save_lanes(runtime, entry, derived)                                                   # S3
   474	    raise_attempts(directory, entry)                                                      # S4
   475	    snapshots = effective_snapshots(directory, applied + [entry])
   476	    finish_repair(runtime, graph, config, entry, fork_run(graph, config, runtime, entry, fork, snapshots))  # S5, S6
   477	    print(f"Repair {entry['n']} applied: {reason}\n{describe(entry, derived, dry_run)}\n  checkpoint forked from {entry['fork_from']} "
   478	          f"(after handoff); nothing launched, no check run\nContinue with: {continuation(runtime)}")
   479

   481	def describe(entry: dict, derived: dict, dry_run: bool) -> str:
   482	    lines = [f"  base: {entry['base_kind']} {entry['base_commit']}"]
   483	    for lane, item in derived["lanes"].items():
   484	        new = f"a commit of tree {item['tree']} on the base" if dry_run else item["commit"]
   485	        lines.append(f"  {lane}: {item['previous_commit']} -> {new}; fix files: {', '.join(item['fix_files'])}; "
   486	                     f"changed files: {', '.join(item['changed_files'])}")
   487	    lines.append("  attempts (each also the floor of its limit): " + ", ".join(f"{key} {value}" for key, value in entry["attempt_targets"].items()))
   488	    return "\n".join(lines)

   497	def make_workspace(runtime, graph, config, lanes: list[str], reason: str | None) -> None:
   498	    """A detached worktree at the base the fix belongs on, with a brief of what blocked the run. No journal, no graph state."""
   499	    directory, repo = runtime.directory, Path(runtime.plan["repository"])
   500	    refuse_recorded(directory)
   501	    applied = applied_repairs(directory)
   502	    _, blocked, _, previous = blocked_run(runtime, graph, config, applied)
   503	    if blocked["packets"][0]["phase"] == "candidate":
   504	        base = read_json(candidate_paths(directory, len(applied))[0])["commit"]
   505	        what = "the combined candidate that failed"
   506	    elif len(lanes) == 1:
   507	        base, what = previous[lanes[0]]["commit"], f"the {lanes[0]} snapshot"
   508	    else:
   509	        raise ValueError("A worker-phase block has no combined candidate: a fix on a lane snapshot repairs one lane only; name one lane")

   540	                                     "frozen lanes blocked at their checks or at the combined candidate, before review. Launches nothing and "

   547	    parser.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true", help="Validate and print what --commit would do; write nothing")
   548	    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

   235	def lane_positions(workers: list[str]) -> tuple[dict, list, int, int]:
   236	    """Report layout: one row per lane for the fan-outs, the fixed tail centred on them."""
   237	    rows = [70 + 140 * index for index in range(len(workers))]
   238	    centre = (rows[0] + rows[-1]) // 2
   239	    positions = {}
   240	    for node, y in zip(workers, rows):
   241	        positions[f"launch_{node}"] = (90, y)
   242	    positions["handoff"] = (280, centre)
   243	    for node, y in zip(workers, rows):
   244	        positions[f"verify_{node}"] = (470, y)
   245	    positions.update(candidate=(660, centre), review=(850, centre), approval=(1040, centre), integrate=(1230, centre))
   246	    edges = [(f"launch_{node}", "handoff") for node in workers] + [("handoff", f"verify_{node}") for node in workers] \
   247	        + [(f"verify_{node}", "candidate") for node in workers] + [("candidate", "review"), ("review", "approval"), ("approval", "integrate")]
   248	    return positions, edges, 1330, rows[-1] + 70

   372	        # Ownership is enforced from the full declared policy: an excluded lane's paths are off-limits to every selected lane.
   373	        excluded_paths = [(other, safe_path(prefix)) for other in self.excluded for prefix in self.worker_policy(other)["owned_paths"]]

   383	    def freeze(self) -> dict:
   384	        record = self.directory / "snapshots.json"
   385	        if record.exists():
   386	            return read_json(record)

   388	        for node in self.workers:
   389	            handoff_path = self.directory / f"{node}.handoff.json"
   390	            if not handoff_path.exists():
   391	                raise ValueError(f"Missing {node} handoff: summary and open_assumptions are required")
   392	            handoff = read_json(handoff_path)
   393	            if set(handoff) != {"summary", "open_assumptions"} or not isinstance(handoff["summary"], str) or not handoff["summary"].strip() or not isinstance(handoff["open_assumptions"], list) or any(not isinstance(item, str) for item in handoff["open_assumptions"]):

   395	            handoffs[node] = handoff
   396	        self.stop_workers()
   397	        snapshots = {}
   398	        for node in self.workers:
   399	            cwd = Path(self.plan["nodes"][node]["worktree"])
   400	            if git(cwd, "rev-parse", "HEAD") != self.plan["base_commit"]:
   401	                raise ValueError("Worker changed HEAD; reconcile commits rather than silently accepting them")
   402	            changed = changed_files(cwd, self.plan["base_commit"])
   403	            self.check_ownership(node, changed)
   404	            for name in changed:
   405	                if (cwd / name).is_symlink():
   406	                    raise ValueError("Symlink changes require manual review before snapshot")
   407	            index = self.directory / f"{node}.snapshot-index"
   408	            if index.exists():
   409	                index.unlink()  # Only our private temporary index, never a user's index.
   410	            env = commit_env()
   411	            env["GIT_INDEX_FILE"] = str(index)
   412	            subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(cwd), "read-tree", self.plan["base_commit"]], env=env, check=True)
   413	            subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(cwd), "add", "-A", "--", "."], env=env, check=True)
   414	            tree = subprocess.check_output(["git", "-C", str(cwd), "write-tree"], env=env, text=True).strip()
   415	            # Validate paths from the actual captured tree, including staged renames/deletes.
   416	            captured = git(cwd, "diff-tree", "--no-commit-id", "--no-renames", "--name-only", "-r", self.plan["base_commit"], tree).splitlines()
   417	            if sorted(captured) != changed:
   418	                raise ValueError("Files changed during snapshot; refuse inconsistent evidence")
   419	            commit = self.plan["base_commit"]
   420	            if changed:
   421	                commit = subprocess.check_output(["git", "-C", str(cwd), "-c", "commit.gpgsign=false", "commit-tree", tree,
   422	                                                  "-p", self.plan["base_commit"], "-m", f"Workflow {self.plan['run_id']}: {node}"], env=env, text=True).strip()

   424	            subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(cwd), "update-ref", ref, commit], check=True)
   425	            receipt = read_json(self.directory / f"{node}.interactive.json")
   426	            snapshots[node] = {"commit": commit, "changed_files": changed, "session_id": receipt["session_id"], **handoffs[node]}
   427	        save_json(record, snapshots)
   428	        self.event("freeze", "succeeded", "Immutable snapshots captured; worker-reported checks are not trusted")

Author: Mani Brar <mani99brar@gmail.com>
Date:   Wed Sep 23 23:46:15 2026 +0000

    repair: a repair whose continuation failed its lane's check again is continued
    
    blocked_run refused any repair while the head was the last repair's fork,
    taking that to mean the run had not continued from it. But a failed verify
    superstep writes no checkpoint: LangGraph keeps the error as a pending write
    on the same checkpoint. So when the first fix was incomplete, or broke the
    lane's own unit check, `automatic --live` (or `retry`) left the fork as the
    head, and both the second repair and `--workspace` were refused with
    "continue with automatic --live", which only hit the identical-failure guard
    again. The run then needed a new run although three repairs are allowed.
    
    The refusal now holds only for a fork nothing has failed from. A repair
    forked from that head passes fork.config, so the pending error and the other
    lanes' pending writes stay on the failed branch, as for the first repair.
    The new test repairs a worker-phase block, fails the repaired lane's check
    twice more, then makes a workspace at repair 1's snapshot, repairs again at
    worker attempt 5 and reaches integration; it also covers the refusal before
    any continuation. The RUNBOOK says when an applied repair can be built on.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

def record_pane_answer(directory: Path, node: str, clock=None) -> dict | None:
    """The session works again while its latest question waits: PANE_ANSWER, and the deadline runs again.

    Checked and written under the lock: when `answer` recorded the answer meanwhile, nothing is recorded (None).
    """
    with question_lock(directory):
        questions = load_questions(directory, node)
        if not questions or questions[-1]["answer"] is not None:
            return None
        at = (clock or time.time)()
        questions[-1].update(answer=PANE_ANSWER, answered_at=iso(at))
        save_questions(directory, node, questions)
        resume_deadline(directory, node, at)
    return questions[-1]


def undelivered_answer(directory: Path, node: str, text: str) -> dict | None:
    """The latest question when `answer` recorded this text but never delivered it: a rerun delivers it, recording nothing.

    A different text is refused: a question is answered once, and its deadline already runs again. So is any rerun once
    the worker went on: the text would reach no question (or a shell).
    """
    questions = load_questions(directory, node)
    if not questions or questions[-1]["answer"] is None or questions[-1].get("delivered") is not False:
        return None
    entry = questions[-1]
    if entry["answer"] != text:
        raise ValueError(f"Question {entry['n']} of {node} is already answered and that answer was never delivered; "
                         f"rerun answer with the recorded text to deliver it: {entry['answer']!r}")
    reason = went_on(directory, node)
    if reason:
        raise ValueError(f"Question {entry['n']} of {node} is answered but that answer was never delivered, and the worker went on from it "
                         f"({reason}); nothing is typed into its pane")
    return entry


def mark_delivered(directory: Path, node: str, number: int) -> None:
    with question_lock(directory):
        questions = load_questions(directory, node)
        questions[number - 1]["delivered"] = True
        save_questions(directory, node, questions)


def deliver_answer(directory: Path, node: str, text: str, use_herdr: bool = True) -> str:
    """Type the answer into the worker's Herdr pane (send-text, then Enter), or say how to type it after `claude attach`."""
    receipt = read_json(directory / f"{node}.interactive.json")
    if not use_herdr:
        return f"Type the answer in the worker's session: claude attach {receipt.get('background_id')}"
    from .herdr import herdr
    terminals = directory / "terminals.json"
    mapping = read_json(terminals) if terminals.exists() else {}  # A run started without --herdr has none.
    if node not in mapping:
        raise RuntimeError(f"No Herdr pane is recorded for {node} in {terminals}")
    pane = mapping[node]["pane_id"]
    herdr("pane", "send-text", pane, text)
    herdr("pane", "send-keys", pane, "Enter")
    return f"Answer typed into pane {pane} ({node})"


# ---- CLI: python -m workflow resume | answer -------------------------------------------------------------------

def resume_main(argv=None):
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="python -m workflow resume", description="Rerun a paused design challenge on the edited feature "
                                     "files, or accept it with a reason; then launch the workers (and supervise an automatic run).")
    parser.add_argument("directory", type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("--accept-challenge", metavar="REASON", help="Record the override with this reason and continue without rerunning")
    parser.add_argument("--herdr", action="store_true", help="Attach the worker panes after the launch")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    directory = args.directory.resolve()
    from langgraph.checkpoint.sqlite import SqliteSaver
    from .pipeline import Pipeline, build_pipeline, graph_config, report, start_workers
    warning = stale_claude_warning()
    if warning:
        print(warning, file=sys.stderr)

    def export(runtime) -> Path:
        """As `start` does on a pause: run-state.json shows the latest attempt and the plan's base and pinned files."""
        with SqliteSaver.from_conn_string(str(directory / "pipeline.sqlite")) as saver:
            return report(runtime, build_pipeline(saver, runtime).get_state(graph_config(runtime)))

    try:
        with run_lock(directory):
            runtime = Pipeline(directory)
            moved = lambda: tuple(path.read_bytes() if path.exists() else None for path in
                                  (directory / "plan.json", directory / "challenge.json", directory / "challenge.running.json"))
            before = moved()
            try:
                record = resume_challenge(runtime, args.accept_challenge)
            except BaseException:
                # A rerun that failed after its re-pin has moved the base and the files: the viewer refuses an export
                # whose base is not plan.json's, and shows the failed attempt's event. A refusal that changed nothing
                # keeps the lock short, so a supervisor's next step is not refused for it.
                if moved() != before:
                    print(f"Report: {export(Pipeline(directory))}")
                raise
            runtime = Pipeline(directory)  # The re-pinned plan on its current base: session receipts bind to its digest.
            if record["status"] == "paused":
                print(paused_message(directory, args.herdr))
                print(f"Report: {export(runtime)}")
                return
            start_workers(runtime, attach=args.herdr)
        print(f"Design challenge {record['status']} (attempt {record['attempt']}); workers launched: {', '.join(runtime.workers)}")
        if runtime.plan.get("automatic"):
            from .automatic import supervise
            try:
                supervise(directory)
            except TransientInfraError as error:
                parser.exit(75, f"Interrupted: {error}\n")  # Resumable, like `automatic --live`.
            print(f"Automatic run reached a verified feature branch. Evidence: {directory / 'report.html'}. No main merge or push.")
    except (ValueError, RuntimeError, OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError) as error:
        parser.exit(1, f"Blocked: {error}\nAll work/evidence retained at {directory}. No automatic fallback or push.\n")


def answer_command(directory: Path, node: str, text: str, herdr: bool = True) -> str:
    return f"{sys.executable} -m workflow answer {directory} {node} {shlex.quote(text)}" + ("" if herdr else " --no-herdr")


def answer_main(argv=None):
    """The deadline restarts when the answer is recorded (PRD 4.6), before the delivery, and stays running when the delivery
    fails: paused until a delivery, it would never run again if the operator then typed the answer in the pane (the
    controller records a pane answer only while the question waits). A rerun delivers the recorded answer within it."""
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="python -m workflow answer", description="Answer a worker's question: record it, restart the "
                                     "worker's deadline and type it into the worker's pane. Rerun it to deliver an answer whose delivery failed.")
    parser.add_argument("directory", type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("node", help="The lane whose latest question this answers")
    parser.add_argument("text")
    parser.add_argument("--no-herdr", action="store_true", help="Print the claude attach command instead of typing into the pane")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    directory = args.directory.resolve()
    entry = delivered = None
    try:
        plan = read_json(directory / "plan.json")
        if args.node not in plan_workers(plan):
            raise ValueError(f"{args.node} is not a lane of this run ({', '.join(plan_workers(plan))})")
        entry = undelivered_answer(directory, args.node, args.text)
        if entry is None:
            entry = record_answer(directory, args.node, args.text, delivered=False)
            print(f"Recorded the answer to question {entry['n']} of {args.node}; its deadline runs again.")
        else:
            print(f"Question {entry['n']} of {args.node} was answered at {entry['answered_at']} and never delivered; delivering it now "
                  "(nothing is recorded again, and its deadline has run since).")
        print(deliver_answer(directory, args.node, args.text, not args.no_herdr))
        delivered = True
        mark_delivered(directory, args.node, entry["n"])
    except (ValueError, RuntimeError, OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError) as error:
        if delivered:
            parser.exit(1, f"Blocked: {error}\nThe answer reached the worker but is not marked delivered; do not rerun answer for this question.\n")
        if entry is not None:
            parser.exit(1, f"Blocked: {error}\nThe answer to question {entry['n']} stays recorded and its deadline runs, but it did not reach "
                           f"the worker. Deliver it by rerunning, from a Herdr pane:\n  {answer_command(directory, args.node, args.text)}\n"
                           f"or print the claude attach command and type it yourself:\n  {answer_command(directory, args.node, args.text, herdr=False)}\n")
        parser.exit(1, f"Blocked: {error}\n")

return path.is_file() and read_json(path).get("status") == "paused"


def command_cwd(command: list[str], target: Path, tool: Path = TOOL) -> Path:
    """`git switch` runs in the target; the `python -m workflow` commands run from the tool's directory."""
    return target if command[0] == "git" else tool


def main(argv=None):
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("feature", help="A directory under <target>/features/ that holds a feature.json")
    parser.add_argument("--repo", type=Path, help="Target Git repository (default: the current directory when it is a Git repository "
                                                  "with features/, otherwise this tool's own repository)")
    parser.add_argument("--run-id", help="Opaque run identifier (default: <feature>-001)")
    parser.add_argument("--run-root", type=Path, help="Run storage outside the target (default: ~/.local/state/md-manager-workflows/<feature> "
                                                      "for md-manager, ~/.local/state/agent-workflows/<repo>/<feature> otherwise)")
    parser.add_argument("--workers", help="Comma-separated subset of the feature's declared lanes to launch (default: every declared lane)")
    parser.add_argument("--live", action="store_true", help="Authorize Claude usage")
    parser.add_argument("--automatic", action="store_true", help="Bypass worker permission prompts; run through independent review to a verified feature branch")
    parser.add_argument("--worker-timeout-seconds", type=int, help="Automatic mode: per-worker deadline from launch to completion signal (default 4h, max 24h)")
    parser.add_argument("--review-timeout-seconds", type=int, help="Automatic mode: reviewer deadline from its launch to its completion file (default 30m, max 24h)")
    parser.add_argument("--reviewer-transport", choices=["native", "print"], help="Automatic mode: native attachable reviewer session (default) or headless claude --print")
    parser.add_argument("--no-herdr", action="store_true", help="Explicitly omit terminal attachments")
    parser.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true", help="Validate feature configuration and print commands and the registry entry only")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    run_id = args.run_id or f"{args.feature}-001"
    try:
        repo = resolve_target(args.repo, Path.cwd())
        feature_folder(repo, args.feature)  # An unknown name is refused with the features found, before anything else.
        run_root = args.run_root or default_run_root(repo, args.feature)
        run, commands, notes = launch_commands(repo, args.feature, run_id, run_root.resolve(), not args.no_herdr, args.automatic,
                                               args.worker_timeout_seconds, args.review_timeout_seconds, args.reviewer_transport, args.workers)
        prepare = commands[2]
        selected = [prepare[index + 1].split("=", 1)[0] for index, item in enumerate(prepare) if item == "--task"]
        reviewers = [prepare[index + 1].split("=", 1)[0] for index, item in enumerate(prepare) if item == "--reviewer"] or ["review"]
        registry = registry_path()
        # The registered graph is the feature's (every declared lane), not this launch's `--workers` subset.
        manifest = load_feature(feature_folder(repo, args.feature))
        declared = [worker["node_id"] for worker in manifest["workers"]]
        challenge = is_guarded(manifest) and manifest.get("challenge", True) is True
        entry = registry_entry(repo, args.feature, run_root.resolve(), declared, challenge=challenge)
        # Before 2.2.0 nothing is refused; the launch says so once, beside (not among) its notes.
        migration = migration_note(manifest)
        if args.dry_run:
            print(json.dumps({"repository": str(repo), "run_directory": str(run), "workers": selected, "reviewers": reviewers, "commands": commands,
                              "executes": False, "notes": notes, "registry": {"path": str(registry), "entry": entry},
                              "guardrails": {"feature_version": manifest["version"], "enforced": migration is None, "challenge": challenge,
                                             "migration_note": migration}}, indent=2))
            for note in notes + ([migration] if migration else []):
                print(f"Note: {note}", file=sys.stderr)
            return
        if not args.live:
            parser.error("Use --live to authorize worker usage, or --dry-run to inspect without running anything")
        if run.exists():
            raise ValueError(f"Run already exists: {run}. Inspect it with status; do not launch duplicate workers.")
        # A malformed registry blocks the launch here, before any Git action; it is never rewritten.
        merge_registry(read_registry(registry), entry)
        for note in notes + ([migration] if migration else []):
            print(f"Note: {note}", file=sys.stderr)
        try:
            for index, command in enumerate(commands):
                subprocess.run(command, cwd=command_cwd(command, repo), check=True)
                if index == 2:
                    # The run directory exists now: make the run visible in the Projects viewer.
                    try:
                        print(f"Projects registry {registry}: {register(registry, entry)}", flush=True)
                    except (ValueError, OSError) as error:
                        print(f"Projects registry {registry} not updated: {error}", file=sys.stderr, flush=True)
                if index == 3 and challenge_paused(run):
                    # `start` printed the concerns and the resume commands; nothing else runs until the operator decides.
                    print(f"\nLaunch paused at the design challenge; no worker was launched. Run: {run}")
                    return
        except KeyboardInterrupt:
            parser.exit(130, f"Launch interrupted. Nothing was rolled back. If workers were started they are still running;\n"
                             f"inspect with: {sys.executable} -m workflow status {run}\n"
                             + (f"resume with:  {sys.executable} -m workflow automatic {run} --live\n" if args.automatic else ""))
        except subprocess.CalledProcessError as error:
            if not (args.automatic and error.returncode == 75):
                raise
            # `automatic` exits 75 when Claude Code itself was unavailable: nothing was stopped and the run is resumable.
            parser.exit(75, f"Launch interrupted: Claude Code was unavailable; nothing was stopped. Once `claude` works,\n"
                            f"resume with:  {sys.executable} -m workflow automatic {run} --live\n")
        if args.automatic:
            print(f"\nAutomatic run finished. Evidence: {run / 'report.html'}. No main merge or push.")
            return
        print(f"\nRun: {run}\nWorkers ({', '.join(selected)}) are in their dedicated Herdr tab (unless --no-herdr).")
        print("Watch/answer permission prompts. When every worker finishes, return to Pi for handoffs and freeze.")
        drill_note = next((note for note in notes if note.startswith("Failure drill skipped")), None)
        if drill_note:
            print(drill_note)
        else:
            folder = feature_folder(repo, args.feature)
            drill = read_json(feature_file(folder, load_feature(folder)["policy"])).get("failure_drill")
            if drill:
                print(f"The intentional {drill['node_id']} verification drill will block its first attempt; retry that check explicitly after restarting the controller.")
        print(f"Status: {sys.executable} -m workflow status {run}")
        print("Review and integration still require separate explicit approval. Nothing is pushed.")
    except (ValueError, OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError) as error:
        parser.exit(1, f"Launch blocked: {error}\nNo fallback, reset or cleanup was attempted. Inspect any retained branch/run state.\n")
    except Exception as error:  # jsonschema ValidationError on the feature file
        from jsonschema.exceptions import ValidationError
        if not isinstance(error, ValidationError):
            raise
        parser.exit(1, f"Launch blocked: feature.json is invalid: {error.message}\nNo fallback, reset or cleanup was attempted.\n")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
